//: Template for the home server. This file is NOT read directly - deploy/install-service.ps1
writes every key below into the Windows service's own environment from deploy/.env (copy
deploy/.env.example there and fill it in; see that file for the exact key list and the
deploy-only keys it also carries). This template exists so every key from
Implementation/01-Architecture.md's Configuration section, plus the deploy-only Kestrel/
AllowedHosts keys, is documented in one place with a placeholder and a comment.
NEVER commit a filled-in copy (appsettings.Production.json is gitignored, but this repo
never uses that file for real deployment - .env is the source of truth). P8-02 owns the
deployment scripts.
Sinks (console + a daily rolling file) are hard-coded in SerilogConfiguration.cs, not
configurable here; only levels/overrides and the directory are. LogDirectory defaults to
<content-root>/logs, which with install-service.ps1's layout is <InstallDir>/app/logs; the
container sets it to /app/logs, a mounted volume (P8-05).
Tailscale HTTPS (README 'Deploy - Tailscale HTTPS'): `tailscale cert <host>.<tailnet>.ts.net`
writes a PEM cert+key pair. Kestrel's `Certificates:Default` accepts a PEM Path/KeyPath pair
(not just .pfx) since .NET 5. This binds every HTTPS endpoint with one cert; ASPNETCORE_URLS
(set in deploy/.env, not here) supplies the actual listen address/port.
Renew monthly with deploy/renew-cert.ps1 (deploy/register-renew-cert-task.ps1 schedules it);
the cert is only trusted by clients on the same tailnet.
D-015. False outside Development by default; deploy/deploy.ps1 runs `dotnet ef database update`
as an explicit step before restarting the service. The Docker deployment sets it to true in
deploy/docker/compose.yaml instead (D-159) - there is no separate deploy step there, and the
image and the migrations it carries are one artifact.
StartupTimeoutSeconds bounds how long startup migration waits for SQL Server to accept
connections before failing fast. Only relevant when MigrateOnStartup is true; an mssql
container takes 20-60 s to come up, and a host reboot starts both containers at once.
P8-05 / D-161. Directory for the ASP.NET Core data-protection key ring, which encrypts the
auth cookie. UNSET on this (Windows service) path: the framework default already lands in a
stable profile directory. The container sets it to /app/keys, a mounted volume, because a
container's own filesystem is discarded on every recreate and a redeploy would otherwise
sign every member out of a season-long cookie.
BootstrapOnStartup is optional (D-164). Left out, it is on when ReferenceData is Cfbd and
Jobs:Enabled is true: the first start on an empty database fetches the season calendar and
the current week's schedule, rankings and lines (about 7 CFBD calls, once). Set false to
leave that to the Tuesday refresh jobs.
Generate once with ./deploy/generate-vapid.ps1 and keep the pair: replacing it invalidates
every stored push subscription. Left as placeholders the app still boots, but
GET /api/push/vapid-public-key answers 503 and no notification is ever delivered.
Subject must be a real mailto: or https: contact.
Push.Subject: mailto:commissioner@example.com

//: BehindProxy (P8-05 / D-160): handle X-Forwarded-For/Proto/Host. FALSE on this path -
Kestrel binds HTTPS itself with the PEM pair above, so there is no proxy and trusting those
headers would let a caller spoof its own client IP past the per-IP rate limiter. The Docker
deployment sets it true because `tailscale serve` terminates TLS on the host and forwards
plain HTTP to a loopback-only container port.
P8-01 / D-153. Fixed window per client IP, one minute wide, on /auth/* and on
/api/invites/{code} + /api/invites/{code}/accept - the only routes a caller can reach
without an existing membership. Over the limit is 429 ProblemDetails with Retry-After.
Leave Enabled true in production; the API test suite sets it false because every in-memory
request shares one partition.

Jobs.//: CatchUpMinutes bounds how much missed schedule a restart replays. Set Enabled false on any second instance.
